message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.71","text":"Nevertheless, brothers, there are some things you should not wait to hear, but should also recognize for yourselves what is reasonable. Is Zacchaeus alone to labor for you? Having given himself over entirely to being occupied, since he has a belly and has no leisure for himself, how can he obtain the necessary food? Is it not reasonable for all of you to take thought for his livelihood, without waiting for him to ask you? For that is the act of a beggar, and he would die of hunger rather than undertake to do this. How, then, will you yourselves not incur punishment if you fail to consider that “the worker is worthy of his wages”? And let no one say, “So then, is the word that was provided freely being sold?” By no means. For if someone who has the means to live should accept support, that person is selling the word. But if someone without the means to live receives food in order to live—as the Lord also received food both at dinners and among friends, possessing nothing though he is the one who will possess everything hereafter—he does not sin. Accordingly, honor elders, catechists, useful deacons, widows who have lived well, and orphans as children of the church. Moreover, whenever a need for some resource for a necessary purpose arises, all of you should contribute together. Act piously toward one another, not hesitating to endure anything at all for the sake of your own salvation.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Ζακχαῖος μόνος ὑμῖν;","chosen":"Is Zacchaeus alone to labor for you?","rationale":"The printed question is elliptical. “To labor” is supplied contextually from the following description of his complete occupation; a more formally literal but obscure alternative is “Is Zacchaeus alone for you?”"},{"source_quote":"ὅλος ἑαυτὸν ἀσχολεῖν ἀποδεδωκώς","chosen":"Having given himself over entirely to being occupied","rationale":"The phrase depicts complete dedication to an occupation or lack of leisure, without specifying a separate office or activity."},{"source_quote":"κοιλίαν ἔχων","chosen":"since he has a belly","rationale":"This preserves the source’s concrete bodily image rather than reducing it to the abstract statement that he has needs."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ζῆν αὐτοῦ πρόνοιαν ποιεῖν","chosen":"to take thought for his livelihood","rationale":"The construction calls for active provision or care concerning the means by which he lives."},{"source_quote":"τοῦτο γὰρ προσαιτοῦντός ἐστιν","chosen":"For that is the act of a beggar","rationale":"The genitive denotes conduct characteristic of one who begs or solicits alms."},{"source_quote":"ἔν τε δείπνοις καὶ φίλοις","chosen":"both at dinners and among friends","rationale":"The two coordinated expressions differ slightly in sense—one denotes occasions and the other company—but both can be retained without emendation."},{"source_quote":"τιμᾶτε","chosen":"honor","rationale":"The immediate context includes material provision, but the verb itself means to honor; the translation does not restrict it to payment alone."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἀλλήλους εὐσεβεῖτε","chosen":"Act piously toward one another","rationale":"The verb denotes the practice of piety or dutiful reverence, here directed toward fellow members of the community."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"Ζακχαῖος μόνος ὑμῖν;","issue":"The confirmed editorial question punctuation leaves the clause without an expressed predicate. The main rendering supplies the idea of labor from the immediately following occupation language; alternatively, the words may be represented more literally as “Is Zacchaeus alone for you?” or ὑμῖν may be understood closely with the following infinitive despite the punctuation. No textual correction is required.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"Ζακχαῖος","issue":"The selected edition spells the name here with one χ but uses Ζαχχαίῳ in 3.72. This is an orthographic variation; both are represented by the conventional English name “Zacchaeus,” without altering the supplied Greek.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.72","text":"After saying these things, he laid his hand on Zacchaeus and said, “Sovereign and Lord of all, the Father and God, you yourself preserve the shepherd together with the flock. You are the cause; you are the power. We are those who receive help; you are the helper, the physician, the Savior, the wall, the life, the hope, the refuge, the joy, the expectation, and the rest. To sum it up, I will say: you are everything to us. Work with us toward the eternal possession of salvation; rescue us; guard us. You can do all things, for you are ruler of rulers and Lord of lords, master of kings. Give the one who presides authority to loose what must be loosed and to bind what must be bound. Make him wise. Through him as through an instrument, preserve the church of your Messiah as a beautiful bride. For yours is eternal glory, the praise of Father and Son and Holy Spirit, throughout all the ages. Amen.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Δέσποτα καὶ κύριε τῶν ὅλων","chosen":"Sovereign and Lord of all","rationale":"“Sovereign” conveys the authority of δεσπότης while distinguishing it from the following κύριος, “Lord.”"},{"source_quote":"σὺ ἡ πρόφασις","chosen":"You are the cause","rationale":"In this prayer πρόφασις is read as the originating cause or ground, rather than its frequent negative sense “pretext.” “You are the ground” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ἡμεῖς τὸ βοηθούμενον","chosen":"We are those who receive help","rationale":"The singular neuter participial expression is treated collectively as the party being helped."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς αἰώνιον ὕπαρξιν σωτηρίας συνέργησον","chosen":"Work with us toward the eternal possession of salvation","rationale":"ὕπαρξις can denote possession, state, subsistence, or existence. “Eternal possession of salvation” gives a coherent objective-genitive sense; “an eternal state of salvation” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"τῷ προκαθεζομένῳ","chosen":"the one who presides","rationale":"The participle literally describes the person seated in front and contextually denotes the community’s presiding leader."},{"source_quote":"σὺ σόφισον","chosen":"Make him wise","rationale":"The unexpressed object is understood from the immediately preceding presiding leader."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ χριστοῦ σου","chosen":"the church of your Messiah","rationale":"χριστός functions independently as a title possessed by God, so its titular meaning is rendered rather than treated as part of a personal name."},{"source_quote":"σοῦ γὰρ ἐστὶν δόξα αἰώνιος, ὕμνος πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ καὶ ἁγίου πνεύματος","chosen":"For yours is eternal glory, the praise of Father and Son and Holy Spirit","rationale":"The rendering takes ὕμνος as an appositional description of the glory. It leaves “praise of” able to express either praise associated with or praise directed toward Father, Son, and Holy Spirit."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς αἰώνιον ὕπαρξιν σωτηρίας συνέργησον","issue":"The relation between ὕπαρξιν and σωτηρίας is interpretively open: the phrase may mean “eternal possession of salvation,” “an eternal state of salvation,” or “eternal existence in salvation.” The main rendering is grammatically and contextually defensible, so no conjecture is needed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"σοῦ γὰρ ἐστὶν δόξα αἰώνιος, ὕμνος πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ καὶ ἁγίου πνεύματος","issue":"The syntax allows ὕμνος to stand in apposition to δόξα, as in the main translation, or to function as a second predicate: “For yours are eternal glory and the praise of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.” The supplied wording supports either construction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"Ζαχχαίῳ","issue":"The selected edition spells the name here with two χ letters, whereas 3.71 has Ζακχαῖος. This nonblocking orthographic variation is represented by the same conventional English name, “Zacchaeus.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.73","text":"After saying these things, he then said, “All of you who wish to be baptized, begin fasting tomorrow, have hands laid on you each day, and inquire about whatever you wish. For I want to remain with you for ten more days.” After three days, when he had begun baptizing, he called me, Aquila, and Nicetas and said, “Since I intend to set out for Tyre after seven days, I want you, after leaving this city, secretly lodging as guests with Bernice the Canaanite, Justa’s daughter, and learning from her precisely the matters concerning Simon, to write to me. For this is of great help to me, so that I may adjust myself accordingly. Therefore, depart from this city in peace.” And so, leaving him baptizing just as he had commanded, we went ahead of him to Tyre in Phoenicia.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Ὅσοι ποτὲ βαπτισθῆναι θέλετε","chosen":"All of you who wish to be baptized","rationale":"Here ποτε gives an indefinite force comparable to “whoever”; it does not require a separate temporal phrase in English."},{"source_quote":"καθ’ ἡμέραν χειροθετεῖσθε","chosen":"have hands laid on you each day","rationale":"In the preparation of baptismal candidates, the passive verb naturally refers to receiving the laying on of hands; “be appointed” is contextually less likely."},{"source_quote":"μεθ’ ἡμέρας ἑπτὰ","chosen":"after seven days","rationale":"The phrase marks the intended interval before the departure for Tyre."},{"source_quote":"ἐξ αὐτῆς ὑμᾶς ἀπελθόντας","chosen":"after leaving this city","rationale":"The feminine pronoun is understood contextually as referring to the current city, Caesarea, rather than to the subsequently named destination, Tyre."},{"source_quote":"λανθανόντως ἐπιξενωθέντας","chosen":"secretly lodging as guests","rationale":"The adverb conveys remaining unnoticed or concealed, while the participle denotes receiving or taking guest lodging."},{"source_quote":"παρ’ αὐτῆς τὰ κατὰ τὸν Σίμωνα ἀκριβῶς μαθόντας","chosen":"learning from her precisely the matters concerning Simon","rationale":"τὰ κατά with a person denotes the facts, circumstances, or matters concerning that person."},{"source_quote":"πολὺ γὰρ μοι συμβάλλεται, ἵνα πρὸς αὐτὸ ἁρμόσωμαι","chosen":"For this is of great help to me, so that I may adjust myself accordingly","rationale":"The neuter singular αὐτό is taken collectively as the matter or situation disclosed by the requested report. A more formally explicit alternative is “so that I may adapt myself to it.”"},{"source_quote":"εἰς Τύρον αὐτὸν προήξαμεν τῆς Φοινίκης","chosen":"we went ahead of him to Tyre in Phoenicia","rationale":"With the personal object αὐτόν, προάγω here means to precede or go ahead of him rather than to lead him."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐξ αὐτῆς","issue":"The feminine pronoun occurs twice without an explicit feminine antecedent in this excerpt. The main translation understands an implicit reference to the current city, Caesarea: “from this city.” A more formally literal rendering is “from it,” and an adverbial sense such as “at once” is less likely but possible. The narrative’s subsequent journey to Tyre supports the chosen contextual referent.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"πρὸς αὐτὸ ἁρμόσωμαι","issue":"The neuter singular pronoun does not directly refer to the masculine Simon and does not formally agree with the preceding neuter plural τὰ. It can nevertheless refer collectively to the matter or situation concerning Simon, yielding “adjust myself accordingly” or “adapt myself to it.” No emendation is necessary.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
